thread:
sara: quick q — we need to finalize the service-account key UX for the org->project rollout. do we want keys to be project-scoped by default or org-scoped?

mike: leaning project-scoped by default. limits blast radius and makes quotas simpler (per-project enforcement). org-scoped could be explicit flag.

julia: product note: customers keep asking for a single key that spans multiple projects for infra scripts. if we force project keys they will create a lot more keys and ask for a dashboard filter.

kevin: security perspective: project-scoped keys are safer. org-scoped keys should require additional consent + audit log + rotation policy. we should also ensure telemetry ties every request to both org_id and project_id when present.

anika: console UX idea: when creating a key let user pick scope: [Project] [Org (requires 2FA + admin consent)]. show an inline warning about quota inheritance.

sara: question: how do we surface quota? currently quota calc uses token owner only. if org key used across projects we need to decide whether to aggregate usage under org quota or attribute to the project that the request targeted.

mike: technical tradeoff: our routing/runtime currently routes by project header (X-Project-ID). We can keep attribution to target project but mark token origin as org. That keeps project-level cost metrics accurate.

julia: ok but customers will expect to see "which service account consumed X tokens" on the billing dashboard. we must add a token-origin column in telemetry.

kevin: also need to support key rotation without traffic loss. propose JWT-style short-lived keys + KMS-backed signing key. service accounts get a long-lived credential that can exchange for short-lived tokens. (see sample exchange)

mike: +1. we should publish the exchange endpoint: 
```
POST /v1/token/exchange
Authorization: Bearer SA_LONG_LIVED
body: {"scope":"project:read write","expiry":300}
```

anika: UX impact: console should show both long-lived creds (rotate/delete) and active short-lived tokens (no UI to copy). also show when a short-lived token was minted and by whom.

kevin: must add audit-bot hook: any long-lived key creation/deletion triggers audit-bot message and requires admin acknowledge for org-scoped.

audit-bot: [audit] key.create org=redwood-inc actor=sara id=sa-key-3 scope=org timestamp=1769754350

sara: one more: backwards compatibility — older SDKs expect API_KEY in header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. do we change header for exchanged tokens? i'd prefer same header so no code changes.

mike: agree, keep Bearer header. differentiate by token type in our auth middleware (kid claim or token prefix).

julia: rollout plan: opt-in beta for org-scoped keys for a few customers, expose telemetry & dashboard filters, then flip default to project-scoped after 2 weeks of feedback.

kevin: gating: admin consent + 2FA enforced on org-scope creation, rotation every 90 days by default. also notify owners 7 days before expiry.

anika: dashboard changes list: (1) show key scope column, (2) add filter by token-origin, (3) show aggregated org quotas if org-scoped keys used. i'll sketch mockups.

mike: infra tasks: add token-origin tag to tracing spans, emit metric token_origin={org,project} so billing pipeline can aggregate. also add server-side enforcement that org-scope keys cannot bypass project-level SLO routing (i.e., we still route by requested project).

sara: sounds good. owners? mike implement auth middleware + exchange endpoint, kevin add audit hooks & rotation policies, anika own console, julia coordinate beta, sara coordinate docs + migration guide.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/auth-exchange v2 -> staging (sha: ab12cd) by mike at 1769754400

mike: i'll open PR with proto and sample curl. will also add flag `org_scope_enabled` behind feature-flag for initial rollout.

julia: timeline: target internal beta next week, public beta in 2 weeks.

sara: ok closing loop — i'll create a doc in /docs/keys with migration steps and link the mockups. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: one last nit — ensure our telemetry preserves PII: strip any user email from audit messages, only store actor_id.

sara: ack, will add note in doc.

mike: moving to tasks list now. thanks.
